description: Issue #899 session-half root cause: every WorkFlow request-path service (WorkflowEngine/WorkflowTimerExecutor via ScopedWorkflowDataContextHolder.Resolve() -> ResolveDataContext, WorkflowDefinitionStore, ProcessDefinitionPublisher) builds its own module DataContext via IWtmDataContextFactory.CreateDC() called with NO tenant argument, so TenantCode was unconditionally null regardless of who was actually asking -- the model-half ITenant/soft-delete query filter (#899, ApplyWorkFlowModels(this)) binds to THIS context instance's own TenantCode, so a migrated multi-tenant consumer's module reads matched ZERO rows. This mutant deletes the fix: ResolveDataContext's `dc.SetTenantCode(ResolveAmbientTenant(sp))` call is replaced with a hardcoded `dc.SetTenantCode(null)`, reproducing the exact pre-session-half-fix behaviour -- the caller's ambient tenant (WTMContext.LoginUserInfo.CurrentTenant) is resolved but discarded, and the DataContext this factory-path branch returns always carries TenantCode == null no matter which tenant scope requested it. Checked against SessionTenantStampingTests899.ResolveDataContext_ScopeWithCurrentTenantA_StampsHolderDataContext, which builds a real prod-like DI container (mirroring ProdDiReproTests.cs), sets a scoped WTMContext.LoginUserInfo.CurrentTenant = 'A', resolves the shared holder DataContext, and asserts its TenantCode == 'A' -- with the mutant applied, TenantCode is null instead and the assertion fails. The green control, ResolveDataContext_BackgroundScopeWithNoLoginUserInfo_TenantCodeStaysNull, asserts that a background scope with no HttpContext/LoginUserInfo ALSO produces TenantCode == null -- proving the mutation does not have broader collateral effects (e.g. breaking DI resolution or the holder itself) beyond the one behaviour it targets: this assertion is true both before AND after the mutant is applied, by design, since the background path's correct value already is null. Mirrors the existing wf899-applyworkflowmodels-processdefinition-tenantfilter-neutralize.json precedent: same red+positive-control test-pair shape, this time targeting the session half's stamping call rather than the model half's filter registration.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.WorkFlow.Test.SessionTen: Without it this holder DataContext's TenantCode stays null regardless of the ambient WTMContext's CurrentTenant

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against the committed baseline (fad1161fb; bin-relative stale demo.db checked for and absent; mutant patch applied via git apply, test run, then reverted via git apply -R): "Assert.AreEqual failed. Without it this holder DataContext's TenantCode stays null regardless of the ambient WTMContext's CurrentTenant."
